recipes.name: Slow Cooker Chicken Chili with Greens and Beans
ingredients_raw: 2 cups canned black beans, rinsed and drained
2 cups canned white beans, rinsed and drained
2 tablespoons chili powder, or more to taste
1 tablespoon garlic and herb seasoning, or more to taste
2 large skinless, boneless chicken breast halves

steps.text: Place black beans, white beans, tomatoes, and kale in a slow cooker.
Melt the butter in a large skillet over medium heat. Stir in the onion; cook and stir until softened and translucent, about 5 minutes.
Transfer the onion to the slow cooker.
Sprinkle with chili powder, garlic and herb seasoning, and salt.
Place the chicken breast halves on top, then pour the chicken broth into the slow cooker.
Cook on Low for 6 hours. Remove the chicken breasts, and shred or cut the chicken into bite-size pieces. Stir the shredded chicken back into the chili.
Stir in the heavy cream, allow to heat for a few minutes, and serve.

raw_recipe.headline: Slow Cooker Chicken Chili with Greens and Beans
raw_recipe.description: Beans, greens, and chicken come together with tomatoes in a thick and creamy broth. This recipe, as with most chili recipes, doesn't need to be exact and can be altered to fit your taste or what you have on hand.

review.reviewBody: Wonderful recipe, and had a followed it, would have been perfect! i didn't have chili powder in my cupboard, neither did i have a can of tomoates. I did add some carrot, celery, and bell peppers though. I also used fresh flowering oriental kale instead of the frozen green. great idea adding kale to the chili! Thank you!!

I made this on the stovetop and had it on the table in less than 40 minutes. I diced my chicken rather than shredding it and I used fresh spinach in place of the kale. So simple to make and quick it you don't use the slow cooker. Thanks for sharing your recipe.

This is a great, versatile recipe. I had a can of seasoned black beans that I used without draining, and then another can of black beans. I used 1 can of white kidney beans and then that was plenty of beans! Used a can of Rotel and a can of stewed tomatoes. I only used 3 cups of liquid and that was more than enough. Threw in some oregano and cumin and it was delicious! I've made this twice - once using kale and once using a combo of swiss chard and spinach. I prefer the kale. I always use fresh and throw it in about an hour prior to dinner time. I don't add the heavy cream.

I really enjoyed this, but hubby complained about the kale while he ate a big bowl... So normal meal times in my house! I modified the recipe based on what I had, but I think still stayed true to recipe. I had dry white beans, so I started them in the crock pot the night before with some chicken broth, and added the onion and garlic (no garlic and herb seasoning), half the chili powder, and a generous amount of cumin. The next morning I proceeded with the recipe as written, adding kale, the rest of the chili powder, etc., and letting it slow cook for about 6 1/2 more hours. I did use fresh kale, about 4 or 5 cups, rather than frozen pre-cooked, and left out the salt because of all the broth I used. Because of dietary issues, I also subbed a brick of softened low fat cream cheese for the cream. Saved on fat, and the blood sugar problems of lactose. I garnished with a shredded queso and sliced avocado. Thanks for sharing! And tho the recipe didn't specify, I did not drain my tomatoes when I added them.

this was very delicious and hearty.. cut the recipe in half and used all white kidney beans, a can of rotel for the diced tomatoes, and about 2 1/2 cups of fresh kale.. didn't saute the onion before adding it in.. used 1 tsp garlic powder and 1 tsp cumin as others did for the garlic and herb seasoning.. reduced the salt to 1/2 tsp.. used two small breasts for the large and left out the heavy cream.. ty so much for the recipe

I thought this was a good recipe for a one pot meal. I substituted fat free evaporated milk for the heavy cream. It has the same thickening/creaming without all the fat. I also only used 3 cups of broth. In addition, I added cumin instead of the herb mix and added corn.

Had to make a few changes: Used 2C broth, added about a cup of frozen corn, cooked fresh kale with the onion, used fresh garlic (cooked with the onion/kale) and my own mix of herbs, and used a can of evap milk instead of cream. This was good, but just a teeny bit bland. It could really use the addition of a jalepeno, or more chili powder, or some hot sauce to bump up the flavor more to our taste. A good way to use kale, though, and it is tasty. My slow cooker was only big enough for 2C of broth and I think it would be too watery for us with 4C anyway.
Loved this. I used corn instead of black beans and did not add the heavy cream. Also used fresh kale. And I made on the stove - not in a slow cooker. Will definitely make again!

I made this tonight for my family and we all loved it. I did not have garlic and herb seasoning so used cumin instead. I omited the heavy cream but served with cheese and sour cream. I used a bunch of fresh turnip greens - instead of chopping them I blended them with some of the chicken stock in my vitamix. Our only "complaint" was that this ended up more watery than we prefer (and I didn't want to transfer it to the stove to reduce it). I think next time I will cut the chicken stock in half. This recipe is definitely a keeper!

I have been wanting to make this for a while. I finally did last night. I turned out better than expected!! 
I did make some changes to the recipe: I add carrot and celery and cooked the veggies and onion in the slow cooker because I wanted all the flavors in the chili (it also made it a one pot dish. instead of using cream to thicken it I pureed halve the beans and added a little corn starch. At the end I added a little brown sugar and cinnamon to make it sweet and spicy. I think the only thing I would change for next time is to add some cream corn to it.

I did the lazy version of this- skipped the sautéed onions and just threw everything else in the crockpot. I used fresh kale and just tore it up into the crockpot. I added a bunch of cayenne and just realized I never added the cream, oops! But this was easy, pretty tasty, and healthy with leaving out the cream.
The recipe is too bland. To create a chili, I added cumin, coriander, and red pepper flakes.
I cooked the beans rather than use canned beans. It took a little longer, but the taste was amazing. I will make it again.

I really liked this. Definitely more of a soup than chili as written but I prefer that. I did use Rotel instead of plain tomatoes and fresh kale instead of frozen but that is the only change I made. I would probably not drain the white beans next time and actually leave the chicken out due to personal preference. Overall a good soup and one worth making again.

I made this as written. It was okay but lacking in flavor. I had to doctor it up with additional seasonings including garlic powder. I then served it with cheese on top. That made it much better. It has potential, so people who like adding their own twist should definitely make this and add all they want.
Was very good. Family didn't care for the spinach but I loved it.
Made this exactly as written, and loved it!
Very easy and very flexible recipe! Tastes great!
This was different but still good. The kale was kind of odd in chili.
We liked this recipe quite well. We sustituted sweet potato cubes for the canned beans and also added green chiles for extra chili flavor. Wonderful!
